description: News ledes for the new core's stories, keyed by the event kind they report (a closure, a death, a filing, a law taking effect, an election result, a council vote, a budget). News sources give patterns only; every part here is a whole sentence said in public-domain federal records (the Congressional Record, hearings, the Federal Register, federal oral histories), with record words as slots.

slots.other-parent: The other parent of a child born to an office-holder, by name, from the birth record.
slots.office-a: An office said as a common noun with its article and realm (a Massachusetts state representative), from the term.
slots.child: The child born, by name, from the birth record.
slots.yeas: The votes for a nominee in the Senate, from the confirmation vote.
slots.nays: The votes against a nominee in the Senate, from the confirmation vote.
slots.starts: The day a law takes effect, as people say it, from the law record.
slots.subject: The business or office that closed, from the event record.
slots.name: A person, by name, from the records.
slots.place: A place, from the place records.
slots.year: A year from the event's date.
slots.date: A date from the event record, as people say it.
slots.number: A count from the event record.
slots.age: An age, computed from the birth record.
slots.pronoun: His, her or their, from the person's record.
slots.pronoun_sub: He, she or they, from the person's record.
slots.office: The office, from the contest record.
slots.wage: An hourly wage, from the law record.
slots.opponent: The other candidate, from the contest record.
slots.percent: A vote share, from the results record.
slots.count: A vote count such as 5 to 2, from the vote record.
slots.measure: The measure, as its record names it.
slots.action: What the body voted to do, from the measure record.
slots.money: A dollar amount, from the budget record.
slots.purpose: What the money is for, from the budget record.
slots.against: How many spoke against, from the hearing record.
slots.body: The governing body, from its record; for a bill's next step, the body the bill is before, from the bill's body office record.
slots.by: Who made the appointment, from its record.
slots.committee: A committee, from the committee record.
slots.crime: An offense, from the charge record.
slots.designation: A bill's designation, as its body numbers it.
slots.family: A family's name, from the household record.
slots.for: How many spoke for, from the hearing record.
slots.from: The amount before, from the law record.
slots.law: The law, as its record names it.
slots.nation: The national rate, from the jobs record.
slots.other: The other parent, by name, from the birth record.
slots.outlet: A newspaper or station, from the press records.
slots.parent: A parent, by name, from the birth record.
slots.party: A party, from the party records.
slots.post: A public post, from the appointment record.
slots.term: A prison term, from the sentence record.
slots.to: The amount now in force, from the law record.
slots.when: The election's date, from the contest record.
slots.issue: A policy question, by its name.
slots.incident: The kind of disaster, from the declaration record.
slots.disaster: The kind of disaster as people say it (lower case), from the incident type on the disaster record.
slots.area: The region a rate is measured for (a metro area, or the state), by name.
slots.unemployment_rate: The country's unemployment rate, as a number of percent, from the macro month record.
slots.wage_growth: How much average hourly pay grew over the year, as a number of percent, from two macro month records.
slots.quote: One sentence of an address, as the record quotes it.
slots.outside: The possessive of the state an area outside its metro areas belongs to ("Kentucky's", "Texas'"), from the regional record.
slots.candidate: A candidate, by name, from the campaign's record.
slots.signatures: How many signed the petition, from the recall's count.
slots.required: How many signatures the law required, from the recall's count.
slots.fewer: How many fewer signed after the member's answer, from the count's reasons.
slots.asker: The citizen who asked a member to carry a bill, by name, from the ask record.
slots.bodies: The bodies that met in the week and took up nothing, listed, from the meeting records.
slots.born: Where a person was born, from the run's birth record, as the place records name it.
slots.employer: The organization a person worked for, from their work record.
slots.survivors: The living partner and children a person leaves, named from their family records, listed.
slots.firm: A business a public contract went to, by name, from the award and the business records.
slots.government: The government a public worker worked for, named from its record (the government of Arizona).
slots.also: A second condition that moved the same month, from the outcome web month record.
slots.jobless: How many residents are looking for work, from the economic month record.
slots.staff: The staff a business plans for or starts with, from its staffing record.
slots.industry: What a business does, from the business books' industry for its kind.
slots.years: How many years a business was open, from its founding date.
slots.ordinal: Which of the month's victimization records of its kind this one is, from the crime month record.
slots.graduates: How many seniors graduated, from the school outcome record.
slots.math: The share of tested students proficient in math, from the school outcome record.
slots.reading: The share of tested students proficient in reading, from the school outcome record.
slots.affordable: How many of the new homes are priced below market, from the project record.
slots.began: The month and year work on a project began, from the project record.
slots.down: The down payment, from the purchase record.
slots.raised: What a campaign has raised in all, from the campaign record.
slots.total: What a donor has given a campaign in all, from the gift record.
slots.majority: The majority leader, by name, from the chamber record.
slots.minority: The minority leader, by name, from the chamber record.
slots.successor: Who takes a vacated seat by law, from the office rule.
slots.before: Who held the seat before, from the seat's earlier term.
slots.owner: A business owner, by name, from the ownership record.
slots.previous: The former owner, by name, from the ownership record.
slots.spending: A government's planned spending for the year, from its budget record.
slots.revenue: The revenue a government expects for the year, from its budget record.
slots.margin: How many votes the winning side led by, from the vote record.
slots.crimes: What most of a month's police reports were (thefts, assaults), from the crime engine's month record.
slots.district: A seat's district, as its seat record numbers it (4, 12A), from the seat records.
slots.commenter: The person a reporter asked for comment, by name, from the comment record.
slots.since: The day a seat fell empty, from the vacancy record.
slots.vacated: The day the seat a new holder takes fell empty, from the vacancy record.
slots.opened: The month and year a business opened, from its founding record, when it was open less than two years.
slots.members: How many sit on a study committee, said in words, from the study's row.
slots.until: The day a study committee reports by, from the study's row.
slots.last: The last name of the person the story already named (an election's winner, an interview's candidate), or full name where another in the story shares it, from the person record.
slots.rival: The runner-up's last name, or full name where another in the story shares it, from the person record.
slots.lasts: The winners of a race for several seats by last name, from the race's count.
slots.winners: The winners of a race for several seats by full name, from the race's count.
slots.seats: How many seats a race filled, in words, from the race's count.
slots.day: The day of the count as the paper says it (on Tuesday, on November 4), from the result record.
slots.field: How many were on the ballot in a race, in words, from the race's count.
slots.short-by: The votes a failed bill lacked for a majority of those cast, as a number, from the vote's yeas and nays.
slots.work: What the endorsing group works for, from the stance its endorsement stood on (the group's own record), as the paper says it.
slots.issue-for: That the candidate answered the interview's headline question for, from the interview's answers.
slots.issue-against: That the candidate answered the interview's headline question against, from the interview's answers.
slots.for-issues: The questions an interview's candidate answered for, each by the name the reporter asked it by, from the interview's answers.
slots.against-issues: The questions an interview's candidate answered against, each by the name the reporter asked it by, from the interview's answers.
slots.declined-issues: The questions an interview's candidate gave no answer on, each by the name the reporter asked it by, from the interview's answers.
slots.plural-subject: Set when the group's name takes a plural verb ("Friends of policing"), from its name's form in data/english/group-names.json.
slots.school: The school the honor row names, from the school's record.
slots.grade: The winner's grade that school year, as a word, from their birth date and the school year.
slots.kin: What the winner is to their parents (daughter, son or child), from the family records.
slots.parents: The winner's parents, by name, from the family records.
slots.a-grade: The winner's grade with its article ('a seventh', 'an eighth'), for 'a seventh grader'.
slots.soon: 'later this month', when the regional bee is held in the month the paper is printed.
slots.usual: How many police reports the town's month usually holds, the mean of its last closed months, from the crime engine's month rows.
slots.extra: How many reports a month ran over the town's usual, from the crime engine's month rows.
slots.rising: The kind of police report that rose most over its own usual that month, from the crime engine's month rows.

mining.rule: A shape is kept when at least 2 documents say it as a whole sentence and one of them is a public-domain record from 2015 or later, which is its source.
